item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
It is most of a decade later and the precaution of no cola allowed in the building still makes no sense.
A similar quibble I don't see anyone pointing out before: why search people for food and beverages when they are entering the area? Shouldn't they be searched when leaving to make sure no one smuggles out any go-go juice? For that matter, why frisk for food at all?

The whole thrust of the containment section seems to be about preventing staff from sneaking a sip. But that's not necessary. Anyone with enough access to know about the super-soda would also know that it kills ugly and fast.

Taking into account issues with containment write-up, I still like this. It's a standard cliché "crank normal thing up to 11" concept, but well executed. And the nasty consequences flow naturally from the effect, not just tacked on random badness for the sake of upping the gore factor.

Plus, much like the zombie plague, it fills a necessary niche. Someone is going to write about super-caffeine, might as well be this version that we keep.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
In addition to removing the need for rest, SCP-207-1 also causes an increase in motor, reaction, and psychological functions. The increase is linear in progression, with an estimated 50% increase (measured by standard medical protocols, +/-5%) every 6 hours. The practical application of ingestion is that the subject is able to think, react, and move faster than others who have not ingested SCP-207-1. Mental proficiencies show the IQ of the subject to rise in line with other increases.

This part seems really vague and distracting, from a statistical/mathematical perspective. Do you mean that all measures, from IQ to muscle strength, grow equally as (1.5)h/6 ? That would be really hard to believe since most of these measurements are human-designed, not comparable with each other, have different standard deviations and means, etc. Is it okay if I rewrite this part to be more precise and better from a scientific perspective? I think I could make it a lot better. (Also, we are talking about exponential growth here, not linear, right? If that's the case, by 48 hours the parameters would go up 26 times. That seems way more than enough to cause death long before that. Reducing the growth rate, changing it to linear, or going into more detail would help make this more believable. )

item.content:encoded: I can understand that, but at the same time, without evidence of it being a hazard, should we start putting things like that in every containment procedure? "Report magical appearance of SCP-xxx outside of its regular containment to supervising researcher immediately." If there was a case of it happening, then I'd think editing the containment procedures to reflect the new "power" would make more sense. Like the cup of gross stuff. It (theoretically) wasn't in the CP to have it on a scale at all times, etc, until it manifested itself outside the containment room.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Ultimately, I think it's a fair precaution. Bear in mind that although we can document these things for months, years, decades, whatever, they are still weird and supernatural. There's no reason to suspect that these bottles would randomly teleport into a vending machine. However, there's no way to be absolutely certain that one day they won't (what if, after 4,000 days without being consumed, they moved themselves to a location in order to be consumed?).

Basically, we don't know for certain what they will do, we only have a reasonable assumption that they won't. It probably won't happen, but it's a precaution that's there just in case it does.

and all personnel entering the area should be checked for any food or drink items, in addition to any other searches required.

All vending machines in Site-██ are to only dispense clear carbonated beverages; any variation from transparent is to be investigated immediately.

It makes it sound like SCP-207 can contaminate other drinks by proximity. If the purpose is to keep people from drinking it, just lock it up in something sturdier than a metal box. The fact that it is invariably fatal in 48 hours or less is a strong deterrent by itself.
